questions.title: Allow only valid service transitions
questions.prompt: Keep the provided Health enum. transition handles starting + "ready" -> ready, ready + "stop" -> draining, and draining + "drained" -> stopped. Every other event leaves the state unchanged. No sockets or services are started by this model.

tests.label: Ready after start
tests.hint: Match both the current state and the event.

tests.label: Stop begins draining
tests.hint: Stopping a ready service begins its drain phase.

tests.label: Cannot skip startup
tests.hint: Reject an event that does not fit the current state.

tests.label: Stopped stays stopped
tests.hint: Do not invent a restart transition.

hints: Each accepted transition needs a state condition and an event condition.
The default result is the current state.
questions.explanation: Explicit transitions keep callers from skipping required phases. The integer results in tests correspond to the enum order: starting=0, ready=1, draining=2, stopped=3.

questions.title: Redact token values in a simple log format
questions.prompt: Replace the value after every literal "token=" with "***". A value ends at the next ASCII space or the end of the string. Preserve all other characters. This is a deliberately narrow log format, not a general secret detector.

tests.label: Middle field
tests.hint: Preserve fields around the redacted value.

tests.label: At end
tests.hint: The end of the string also ends a value.

tests.label: Empty value
tests.hint: Even an empty value gets the replacement marker.

hints: Find the marker, then find the next space after it.
Replacement changes the string length, so advance using the replacement length.
questions.explanation: The scan follows the stated field boundary rather than trying to guess secrets. Real logging should avoid emitting sensitive fields in the first place and use a structured redaction policy.

questions.title: Cap exponential retry delay without overflow
questions.prompt: Start at min(base, cap). Double once per failure, stopping at cap. Return zero when base or cap is zero. Avoid unsigned overflow, even for a very large failure count. This deterministic calculation omits jitter on purpose.
questions.signature: std::size_t retryDelay(unsigned failures, std::size_t base, std::size_t cap)

tests.label: No failures
tests.hint: The initial delay is not doubled yet.

tests.label: Cap reached
tests.hint: Saturate rather than exceeding the cap.

tests.label: Huge count
tests.hint: Stop growing once the cap is reached.

hints: Before doubling, compare delay with cap/2.
Once delay reaches cap, later failures cannot change the answer.
questions.explanation: Saturating growth prevents a large unsigned value from wrapping into a short delay. The early stop also avoids looping through a huge failure count.
